sources.title: Human History Map civilization index
sources.note: Exact hejaz 600 to 800 and hejaz-1920 1920 to 1945 records, names, approximate dates, and imported-map identity.

sources.title: Human History Map imported summaries
sources.note: Byte-identical imported summaries connect both ids to the historical region; retained only as atlas metadata, not as historical authority.

sources.title: Human History Map research coverage registry
sources.note: Exact missing-card status, observed intervals, border counts, and unreviewed identity, chronology, and border fields.

sources.title: Human History Map 500 borders
sources.note: Pre-start seam control before the early regional feature appears.

sources.title: Human History Map 600 borders
sources.note: First exact hejaz feature, decoded polygon, representative point membership, and geometry hash.

sources.title: Human History Map 700 borders
sources.note: Second exact hejaz feature, identical decoded geometry, and overlapping caliphal layers.

sources.title: Human History Map 800 borders
sources.note: Early endpoint seam where the regional feature disappears and broad Abbasid coverage replaces it.

sources.title: Human History Map 900 borders
sources.note: Post-early control confirming the regional id remains absent.

sources.title: Human History Map 1914 borders
sources.note: Pre-modern seam control showing Ottoman and other atlas assignments before hejaz-1920 appears.

sources.title: Human History Map 1920 borders
sources.note: First exact hejaz-1920 feature, decoded polygon, representative point membership, and geometry hash.

sources.title: Human History Map 1930 borders
sources.note: Second exact hejaz-1920 feature, identical decoded geometry despite the 1925 political conquest.

sources.title: Human History Map 1938 borders
sources.note: Third exact hejaz-1920 feature layered with Saudi Arabia after the 1932 state renaming.

sources.title: Human History Map 1945 borders
sources.note: Endpoint seam where the regional layer disappears while Saudi Arabia continues.

sources.title: Human History Map 1960 borders
sources.note: Post-end control confirming continuing Saudi state coverage without the hejaz-1920 overlay.

sources.title: A History of Saudi Arabia, sample chapter
sources.note: Cambridge University Press historical synthesis distinguishing the Hijaz as a diverse western region, the sharifian order, towns, tribes, pilgrimage, and later Saudi incorporation.

sources.title: The Constitution of Medina and the community of believers
sources.note: Brill scholarly chapter treating the early Medinan compact, its groups, obligations, and historical limits soon after the Hijra.

sources.title: The Holy City of Medina
sources.note: Cambridge scholarly history of Medina as a sacred, legal, and political center under changing early Islamic authorities.

sources.title: Kufa and classical narratives of early Shiism
sources.note: Cambridge scholarship on Ali making Kufa his caliphal capital in 656 and the political consequences of that move.

sources.title: Setting the Stage
sources.note: Cambridge synthesis locating the Umayyad political center in Damascus from 661.

sources.title: The Caliphate of Ibn al-Zubayr
sources.note: Peer-reviewed Brill study of Ibn al-Zubayr and Mecca during the second civil war, 683 to 692.

sources.title: The Umayyad Empire
sources.note: Cambridge political history covering Abd al-Malik, the second civil war, restored Umayyad control, pilgrimage politics, and Hijazi relations.

sources.title: The Hajj Pilgrimage Routes: The Darb Zubaydah
sources.note: UNESCO account of the Kufa to Mecca pilgrimage road, Abbasid investment, stations, wells, pools, dams, markets, and water engineering.

sources.title: The Syrian Hajj Road
sources.note: UNESCO account of the Damascus to Medina pilgrimage route, its stations, inscriptions, and long service to pilgrims and travelers.

sources.title: Archaeology and material culture
sources.note: Cambridge overview explaining archaeological possibilities and the exceptional access limits around the holy cities.

sources.title: The inscription of Zuhayr, the oldest Islamic inscription
sources.note: Peer-reviewed edition and translation of the 24 AH rock graffito between al-Ula and Hegra.

sources.title: Documentary heritage of AlUla
sources.note: UNESCO presentation of the Zuhayr inscription with Arabic text, location, date, and historical significance.

sources.title: Medieval Islamic Medicine
sources.note: Scholarly NCBI Bookshelf edition discussing early medical narratives and warning that later literary accounts are uneven evidence for seventh-century practice.

sources.title: Western Arabia and Yemen to the Ottoman conquest
sources.note: Cambridge regional history of post-Abbasid western Arabia, local sharifian authorities, and changing outside powers.

sources.title: Saudi Arabia and the Gulf states from the First World War
sources.note: Cambridge account of the Hashemite kingdom, Saudi conquest, and the new political order after 1925.

sources.title: Worldmaking in the Hijaz, 1919 to 1926
sources.note: Peer-reviewed study of diverse Hijazi communities, international Muslim debates, and political change from Hashemite rule through Saudi conquest.

sources.title: From Paris to Taif: sovereignty, borders, and minorities
sources.note: Peer-reviewed analysis of the 1916 kingdom, international recognition, territorial claims, and the sovereignty shift after conquest.

sources.title: Memories of the Beloved: oral histories from the siege of Medina
sources.note: Peer-reviewed oral-history study of civilian families, forced movement, hunger, and memory during the 1916 to 1919 siege.

sources.title: Foreign Relations of the United States, 1942, Near East and Africa
sources.note: Official United States diplomatic record reviewing 1924 hostilities, the displacement of Hussein, conquest, and the 1927 Treaty of Jeddah.

sources.title: Treaty of Jeddah, 1927
sources.note: League of Nations Treaty Series primary text recognizing the complete independence of the dominions of Ibn Saud and his title as King of the Hejaz and Nejd and Dependencies.

sources.title: History of Saudi Arabia
sources.note: Official Embassy of Saudi Arabia chronology for the 1926 kingship, dual realm, and 1932 proclamation of the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia.

sources.title: History of the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia
sources.note: Saudi Ministry of Foreign Affairs chronology for unification, the 1932 state name, and Saudi participation in 1945 international institutions.

sources.title: Historic Jeddah nomination dossier
sources.note: UNESCO nomination dossier documenting Jeddah tower houses, pilgrim lodging, mixed commercial and domestic buildings, and the early twentieth-century urban fabric.

sources.title: Historic Jeddah ICOMOS evaluation
sources.note: ICOMOS assessment of Jeddah architecture, privacy, coral-stone tower houses, street life, coffeehouses, squares, and social spaces.

sources.title: Economic lifelines of Jeddah: trade and pilgrimage
sources.note: Cambridge history of merchants, guides, water, sanitation, public health, and livelihoods tied to port trade and pilgrimage.

sources.title: The traditional house of Jeddah
sources.note: University of Edinburgh doctoral research recording rooms, ventilation, privacy, cleaning, stacked latrines, sewage ducts, septic tanks, and annual emptying.

sources.title: Reports on the pilgrimage to Mecca, 1929
sources.note: British Library Qatar Digital Library primary administrative reports on pilgrimage declarations, shipping disruption, and cholera concerns in 1929.

sources.title: Sanitary rules for pilgrim ships, 1925
sources.note: British Library Qatar Digital Library primary file on ship sanitation, inspections, notices, and rules affecting pilgrims traveling to the Hijaz.

sources.title: International Sanitary Convention, official record
sources.note: WHO official record preserving international sanitary provisions for pilgrim ships, inspections, quarantine, and vaccination.

sources.title: Water supply in Ottoman and early modern Jeddah
sources.note: Peer-reviewed historical study of chronic potable-water scarcity for Jeddah residents, troops, and pilgrims.

sources.title: Schooling women in Saudi Arabia
sources.note: Cambridge scholarship noting Hijazi advocacy for girls education during the 1920s and the gap between public argument and later state provision.

sources.title: Al-Falah Schools historical record
sources.note: Institutional history of the Al-Falah boys schools founded in Jeddah in 1905 and Mecca in 1912, with free religious and modern subjects.

sources.title: Education in the reign of King Abdulaziz
sources.note: Official Saudi reference on early state educational institutions, including the Islamic Institute in Mecca in 1926.

sources.title: The postage stamps of the Hejaz, Jeddah and Nejd
sources.note: Library of Congress digitization of a 1927 specialist monograph reproducing and explaining the 1922 Hashemite government inscription on Hejaz stamps.

sources.title: Saudi Arabia: United Nations member state
sources.note: Official United Nations member-state record giving Saudi Arabia admission on 24 October 1945.

sources.title: The Hejaz Railway
sources.note: UNESCO account of the Damascus to Medina railway, pilgrimage travel, stations, and its historical setting.
